sentence: We present the case of a 20-year-old patient who attended the Faculty of Dentistry of Seville referred by her orthodontist.

Given the inadequate position of the lower left canine (including in a horizontal position), the temporary canine was used by the orthodontist during orthodontic treatment as a permanent tooth, not considering it appropriate to rescue the permanent tooth.
She informed the patient of the existence of the dental inclusion and the need for extraction or at least monitoring it.

In the radiological examination (orthopantomography) we confirmed the inclusion of the lower left canine in a horizontal position under the apices of the premolars and contralateral lower canines (transmigration pattern 4 of Mupparapu (8)).
Given the evidence of the transmigration of the canine, we indicated its extraction.

If we continued to control the case, as the impacted tooth approached the mental foramen, the risks of the intervention would be unnecessarily increased, while clinical symptoms would almost certainly occur due to irritation of the lower dental nerve by the impacted tooth (9 , 10).
The extraction was performed through a partial Neuman incision, with discharge at the level of the left lateral incisor.
No unloading was performed in the fourth quadrant due to the proximity of the mental foramen, identifying and protecting the right mental nerve during the intervention.
The tooth was extracted by coronal osteotomy and double odontosection, also eliminating the pericoronary sac.

Finally, the wound was sutured and analgesic, anti-inflammatory treatment (Ibuprofen 600 mg, 1 tablet / 8 hours for a week) and antibiotic treatment (Amoxicillin 875 mg / Clavulanic acid 125 mg, 1 tablet / 8 hours for a week) was prescribed for the postoperative period, which passed without incident.
The stitches were removed after ten days.
The evolution was favorable without any complications detected.
